columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Built for online schools, accelerators, incubators, paid communities, innovation hubs, support groups, and similar community businesses.

Core stack: real-time chat + threaded discussions, static and cohort courses, in-person/virtual events, content library, member directory, matchups, access groups, payments (subscriptions + digital products), landing pages, automated workflows, affiliates, email/DM sequences.
Communities run under your own domain; Heartbeat provides the underlying communication and community stack.
Multiple paid tiers unlock payments, workflows, affiliates, and other advanced features.

strengths.title: Comprehensive community business stack
strengths.detail: Chat, courses, events, content, payments, landing pages, and workflows in one product, less tool sprawl.

strengths.title: Real-time interactions plus structured content
strengths.detail: Live chat alongside courses and libraries, ongoing community and curriculum together.

strengths.title: Built-in payments and automation
strengths.detail: Native subscriptions, digital products, affiliates, and email/DM workflows for monetization and ops.

strengths.title: Own-domain presence and branding
strengths.detail: Runs on your domain, positions the community as a standalone property, not a social-network subspace.

weaknesses.title: Heavier than pure chat apps
weaknesses.detail: Rich feature set can be overkill for small informal groups that only need messaging.

weaknesses.title: Learning curve for complex setups
weaknesses.detail: Courses, events, workflows, and payments need more setup and ongoing management than simpler platforms.

weaknesses.title: Less mainstream than incumbents
weaknesses.detail: Smaller ecosystem and fewer third-party resources than Slack, Discord, or Facebook Groups.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Heartbeat is community platform for cohort-based and branded online communities, chat, events, and memberships. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Heartbeat is an all-in-one platform for community businesses that lets you host chats, live events, courses, content, payments, and workflows under your own domain. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Heartbeat side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Heartbeat you can use Community & Messaging as a first-class product job. The job is hanging out, announcements, and live conversation, not packaging knowledge into something strangers can browse later.

Using Kahana with Heartbeat

You can use both. Heartbeat keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep live conversation on Heartbeat. Pin a Kahana hub or Club link in a channel, discuss live there, and assign the next ebook, video, or course from Kahana so the syllabus is not buried in the thread.
